_comment: Config for H100 20GB nerf_ds dataset, NO masks (ignore_mask=true, forces the Otsu motion-threshold freeze_background_motion). Revised 2026-10-17 after a real full_eval.py run on this exact GPU: as_novel_view finished 40000 iters in 4h23m (over the 2-3h target) at anchor_stride=4/M=213 peak; basin_novel_view and bell_novel_view both hit 'NVML_SUCCESS == r INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED ... CUDACachingAllocator' (a VRAM-exhaustion crash) at N=230-290k Gaussians while M was still mid-refine (111-168) and BEFORE/just-after the Otsu freeze -- i.e. the worst-case window where N (dense Gaussians, still growing via densification) and M (anchor count) are both large simultaneously. Fix mirrors the already-H100-tested configs_hypernerf.json recipe but goes further (anchor_stride 8 not 6, knn_k 32 not 40) since 20GB is half of the 40GB that config assumed and nerf_ds's observed Gaussian counts here (up to 286k) are larger than expected: anchor_stride 4->8 and coarse_levels 3->2 (drops the costly 213-anchor finest level entirely -- bell's own log shows M=111 at stride 8, which is exactly where it crashed transitioning toward 213), knn_k 48->32 (cuts the per-iteration O(N*K) _mls_correct/transport-fit cost, which is where bell's crash stack trace originated), densify_grad_threshold 0.0006->0.0009 and densify_until_iter 16000->12000 (curbs runaway Gaussian growth -- N hit 286k by iter 8000 under the old settings), dyn_select_iter moved earlier (9500->7000, now BETWEEN the two anchor_refine_iters instead of after) to shrink the dynamic-Gaussian tensor via background freeze sooner, reducing peak N*M memory even though the Otsu motion signal is slightly less refined. iterations cut 40000->20000 (as_novel_view's own 4h23m/40000-iter run implies ~2h11m for 20000 at the old slower settings; the above memory/compute cuts should make per-iteration speed similar or better, giving comfortable headroom under 2-3h). If NVML/allocator crashes recur, also try setting env var PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True before training, and/or cut anchor_stride further / densify_grad_threshold higher still.
